title: How far did the godwit fly each day and every hour?
description: A flight of thirteen thousand five hundred sixty kilometres over about eleven days is divided first by the days and then by the twenty four hours in a day. Both results are rounded and then multiplied back to check them.
teaching_notes: One idea: divide by days for the distance each day, then by twenty four for the distance every hour. Watch for students who divide the whole distance by eleven again for the hours.

source: A bar-tailed godwit holds the record for the longest recorded non-stop flight. It travelled 13,560 km from Alaska to Australia without stopping. Its journey started on 13 October 2022 and continued for about 11 days. Find out the approximate distance it covered every day. Find out the approximate distance it covered every hour.
video_script.why: The child divides a long distance by a number of days, and now divides again to get the distance for one hour.
video_script.substitution: Divide the whole distance by the number of days, then divide that daily distance by the twenty four hours in a day.
video_script.anchor: a bar-tailed godwit flying from Alaska to Australia, with the distance 13,560 km and the time about 11 days marked
video_script.payoff_line: Divide by the number of days for each day, then by twenty four for each hour

final_answer.value: About 1233 km each day and about 51 km each hour
final_answer.spoken: about one thousand two hundred thirty three kilometres each day and about fifty one kilometres every hour

maths_rules: a day has 24 hours; distance each hour = 1233 / 24 = 51.4, about 51 km
video_script.design: One idea: divide by days for each day, then by twenty four for each hour. The godwit and the flight stay in the anchor band; the working band shows the two divisions and the check. No hard clear.

<bookmark mark='m2'/>A bar-tailed godwit holds the record for the longest non-stop flight.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>It flew thirteen thousand five hundred sixty kilometres from Alaska to Australia.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>The journey took about eleven days.
<bookmark mark='m5'/>About how far did it fly each day, and about how far every hour?

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>We have to find the distance flown each day and every hour.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, divide the whole distance by the number of days.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The division gives one thousand two hundred thirty two and a bit more.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>That rounds to one thousand two hundred thirty three kilometres each day.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, a day has twenty four hours.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>One thousand two hundred thirty three divided by twenty four is a little more than fifty one.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>That rounds to fifty one kilometres every hour.

marks.m1: the heading check by multiplying appears

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, check by multiplying back.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Fifty one times twenty four is one thousand two hundred twenty four.
That is close to one thousand two hundred thirty three.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>One thousand two hundred thirty three times eleven is thirteen thousand five hundred sixty three.
That is close to the whole flight.

beats.on_screen: Answer: About 1233 km each day and about 51 km each hour
